study type: Cohort study with a case-control design (follow-up study)
exposure: Hypoxic-ischemic (HI) brain injuries in full-term neonates detected during neurosonography
Moderate brain edema and/or thalamus and/or basal ganglion injuries along with cerebellum and brainstem (E/T/BG/C/B) injuries
Moderate brain swelling (edema) and thalamus and/or basal ganglion (E/T/BG) injuries
outcome: Mental development outcomes at an early school age
Neuromotor development outcomes at an early school age
cohort: The study cohort consisted of 32 8-9-year-old children who experienced hypoxia at birth with mild to moderate HIE and a control group of 16 healthy 8-9-year-old children, all of whom had undergone cerebral ultrasonography within the first five days of life.
finding: Moderate hypoxic-ischemic brain changes detected during ultrasonography were statistically significantly associated with hearing disorders, cerebellar dysfunction, epilepsy, and a lower Working Memory Index in children at an early school age.
